 Amy Yasbeck Reveals the Daily Routine Keeping John Ritter’s Memory Alive Two Decades After His Sudden Passing 
 In this story 
 The Tragic Misdiagnosis That Cut Ritter’s Life Short 
 A Tireless Mission to Save Other Families 
 Remembering the Man Behind the Laughter 
 More than two decades after the tragic loss of sitcom icon John Ritter , his widow, Amy Yasbeck, still talks to him every single day. The 64-year-old actress revealed that she continually checks in with her late husband, keeping his warmth and comedic presence interwoven into her family’s daily life.
 Yasbeck and Ritter’s adult children—Jason, Carly, and Tyler, from his first marriage, alongside their child, Noah—regularly bond over the exact type of physical humor and sharp comedy that Ritter mastered throughout his career.
 Whenever a brilliant new stand-up comedian emerges or an actor executes flawless physical comedy, the family instantly feels his presence in the room.
 Amy Yasbeck. 
 John Ritter and Amy Yasbeck. 
 “John was such a good audience,” Yasbeck recalled, noting how much he treasured the craft from both sides of the curtain. “He loved being on stage. He loved to be in an audience.”
 The Tragic Misdiagnosis That Cut Ritter’s Life Short
 The pair first crossed paths during a 1990 table read for the comedy classic Problem Child . After welcoming Noah in 1998, they married the following year, forming one of Hollywood’s most beloved partnerships.
 That life together came to a devastating halt in September 2003. While rehearsing on the set of his hit ABC sitcom 8 Simple Rules for Dating My Teenage Daughter , the 54-year-old actor suddenly suffered intense chest pains.
 Emergency medical personnel rushed Ritter to a nearby medical center, where doctors initially misidentified his symptoms and began treating him for an acute heart attack.
 Amy Yasbeck and John Ritter. 
 Amy Yasbeck and John Ritter. 
 The true culprit behind the collapse was not a coronary blockage, but an aortic dissection —a tear in the inner layer of the body’s main artery. Ritter tragically passed away that same night.
 Busting the Heart Attack Myth: Understanding Aortic Dissections
 A widespread public misconception equates sudden chest agony strictly with traditional heart attacks. In reality , aortic dissection is a distinct, surgical emergency requiring vastly different emergency protocol.
 Administering standard blood-thinning treatments intended for heart attacks can prove fatal during an aortic tear, making rapid, precise diagnosis vital for survival.

 A Tireless Mission to Save Other Families
 Determined to spare other households from sudden grief, Yasbeck launched the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health just weeks after losing her husband. The organization focuses on spreading critical awareness about the warning signs and inherited genetic markers linked to thoracic aortic disease.
 “You can remember John, everybody remembers John. It’s not about that. It’s [about] losing somebody in your family to something that was preventable. … The fact that it’s highly genetic.”
 Yasbeck continues to champion the foundation’s work through major cultural celebrations. She partnered with Ritter’s former Three’s Company co-star Joyce DeWitt for a milestone 50th-anniversary celebration at Joe’s Pub in New York City, complete with an all-star celebrity staged reading featuring Jason Biggs, Christine Taylor, Richard Kind, Susie Essman, and Richard Kline.

 Don Knotts and John Ritter. 
 Remembering the Man Behind the Laughter
 Decades later, fans still stop Yasbeck on the street almost every day to recount how much the comedy legend impacted their childhoods and family living rooms.
 Yet for Yasbeck, the most irreplaceable part of Ritter was not his comedic timing or his Hollywood status—it was witnessing his deep commitment to fatherhood.
 John Ritter and Amy Yasbeck. 
 Three’s Company cast members. 
 “That encompasses everything. His humanity, his comedy, his empathy, his frustration at the world.”
 She remembered him as an intensely fair-minded, progressive protector who could not tolerate seeing children mistreated or overlooked. That boundless empathy remains the defining trait his family honors every day.
 ✨ John Ritter brought uninhibited joy to generations of television viewers, and his family continues to turn their deepest heartbreak into lifesaving public awareness.
